rationale:
The example `requirements.sdk.graph.search.utf8_window` describes a concrete case. A file-root item holds `éhit猫` with no header or trailer. With `window_bytes: 2` the excerpt is `éhit...`. With the default window it is `éhit猫`.

The `{test}` reference is `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[root_hits_clip_context_to_utf8_boundaries]`. Its second loop iteration uses source `éhit猫`, pattern `hit` and a file named `fragment.rs`. The test fixture `project` builds a single-text project. The source is written as the whole file, and the hit is in the file-root node `fragment.rs#`, so the item has no header or trailer.

Each expected outcome is asserted:
- **Small window:** `search_text` is dispatched through `SessionTools` with `{"pattern":"hit","window_bytes":2}`. The test asserts that the page's `matches` equal `[{"tag":"1","node":"fragment.rs#","excerpt":"éhit..."}]`. This checks the whole `é` retained before the hit. It also checks that the 3-byte `猫` is dropped, because the 2-byte window would split it and the boundary moves inward. Finally it checks that the `...` marker is inserted at the end cut.
- **Default window:** The same assertion with no `window_bytes` expects the full `éhit猫`. The retained spans cover the item, so the excerpt is the original text.
- **Extras:** The test also reads the node back and checks that the full source is returned.

The example's JSON shows `node` as `{"File":"fragment.rs"}`, while the test asserts the string form `"fragment.rs#"`. The text does not say the example's JSON is an exact wire format. The test uses the project's actual node representation, so I don't count this as a gap.

The test covers the scenario and every stated outcome. It also checks the cited `windows` and `omissions` behaviour for this case. I found no gap.

text: A file-root item contains `éhit猫` and has no header or trailer. With `window_bytes: 2`, the agent receives `{"tag":"1","node":{"File":"fragment.rs"},"excerpt":"éhit..."}`. The two bytes before `hit` contain the entire `é`. The two bytes after it cover only part of `猫`, so the excerpt ends with the omission marker. With the default window, the excerpt is `éhit猫`.

The agent's `search_text` tool accepts a nonnegative `window_bytes`, defaulting to 128. For a hit with byte span `[start, end)`, retain the hit and up to `window_bytes` of source immediately before `start` and after `end`. Clip the window to the enclosing item's span. Move a context boundary that splits a UTF-8 character inward to the nearest character boundary. With `window_bytes: 0`, only the hit spans and the available header and trailer contribute source to the excerpt.

Compute windows for all hits in the item from the same snapshot. Where windows touch or overlap, emit the contiguous source once. This preserves each hit and the text between nearby hits, including whitespace and newlines.

Render the union of the header, hit windows, and trailer in source order. Copy retained bytes verbatim and replace each nonempty omitted region of the enclosing item with the literal `...`, including a gap at the beginning or end. Insert the marker directly at the cut. When the retained spans cover the item, the excerpt is its original text.
